website.note: Primarily a commercial regenerative medicine / wound care company; clinical pipeline summarized via 10-K

no_active_clinical_pipeline_reason: Organogenesis is a commercial-stage regenerative medicine / wound care company. Most marketed products are FDA-cleared/approved devices and 361 HCT/Ps (Apligraf, Dermagraft, PuraPly, Affinity, NuShield, NovaChor, etc.) and are not active clinical trials. The single late-stage clinical-trial asset is ReNu (amniotic suspension allograft) for knee OA — both Phase 3 trials are completed; rolling BLA submission in progress (initiated post Type B FDA meeting Dec 2025).

pipeline.modality: Cryopreserved suspension derived from human amniotic membrane and amniotic fluid cells; intra-articular injection

indications.highest_phase: Phase 3 complete; rolling BLA in progress
indications.trial_name: ReNu Phase 3 ASA Knee OA program (two pivotal trials)
indications.trial_design: Prospective, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, saline-controlled; single IA injection. Trial 1: completed Q2 2024 (met primary, p=0.0177 pain reduction; p<0.0001 function). Trial 2: 594 patients, completed Aug 2025; missed primary (p=0.0393 vs target 0.023) but numerical improvement and favorable safety.
indications.trial_status: Both Phase 3 trials completed; rolling BLA submission initiated; expected complete H1 2026. RMAT designation granted.
key_milestones: Dec 2025: FDA Type B meeting confirmed BLA pathway
H1 2026: Rolling BLA submission completion targeted

commercial_product.note: Substantial commercial portfolio (Apligraf, Dermagraft, PuraPly/PuraPly AM, NuShield, Affinity, Novachor, CYGNUS, SimpliMax, PuraForce, FortiShield 510(k), TransCyte) — outside active P1/P2/P3 scope.
